links.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot orthodontic retention responses versus recommended patient education thresholds
links.effect: FRE indicated difficult readability; FKGL corresponded to high school- to college-level reading grade; no difference among chatbots (p > 0.05).
links.quote: However, all responses were written at a readability level exceeding recommended thresholds for patient education materials, which may limit their practical usefulness.

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot responses relative to recommended patient education levels
links.effect: FKGL scores corresponded to a high school- to college-level reading grade; all responses exceeded recommended readability thresholds.
links.quote: No difference in FRE and FKGL scores was found among the chatbots (p > 0.05), with FRE scores indicating difficult readability, while FKGL scores corresponded to a high school- to college-level reading grade.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the response quality and readability of three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) on orthodontic retention questions for patients, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
